newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TO REINSTATE FOOTWEAR IMPORT CONTROLS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TO REINSTATE FOOTWEAR IMPORT CONTROLS.

text.p: South Africa plans to reinstate quantative import controls for a year on footwear originating in non-World Trade Organisation countries from April 1, the trade and industry department said on Wednesday.

The department said the measure was introduced because of the "exceptional circumstances" surrounding the footwear industry and will result in maximum benefits for workers, consumers, retailers, producers and suppliers of raw materials.

"In order to allow the local footwear industry time to restructure...the minister (Alec Erwin) proposed, after consultation with all stakeholders, the re-instatement of quantative import controls on footwear originating in non-WTO countries for one year," the department said in a statement.
It said this will give the local industry time to restructure, including ugrading its technology and retraining workers so as to be internationally competitive.
The department said footwear imported from non-WTO members had increased to 40 million pairs in 1996 from 25 million pairs in 1994. This had resulted in job losses of about 3,000.
It said the quantative control should not be interpreted as a move away from international trade or as dependence on customs tariffs to protect local industry.
It added that no protection would be available on demand and that the move was aimed at ensuring "sustainable employment in the face of unfair competition."
